Performance of the Week: Detroit Catholic Central's Zacchaeus Brocks

May 15, 2026

Share This Story
Facebook
Twitter
WhatsApp
SMS Text Message
Email
Print
Copy Link to Clipboard

Copy link

Click below to copy the link to your clipboard

Zacchaeus Brocks ♦ Detroit Catholic Central
Senior ♦ Track

Brocks, who has rebounded from injuries both midway through last season and before the start of this spring's outdoor schedule, set Catholic High School League Championships records Saturday in both hurdles races. In just his second meet of the season, Brocks won the 110-meter hurdles in 13.26 seconds and the 300 hurdles in 36.75. The 110 time is the third-fastest in the country this season according to Athletic.net, and the 300 time is ranked 23rd nationally. 

After finishing runner-up in the 110 hurdles and seventh in the 300 hurdles at the Lower Peninsula Division 1 Finals as a sophomore, Brocks saw his junior season end in early May because of a stress fracture in a toe. He came back strong during this winter's indoor season and ran the 60-meter hurdles in 7.44 seconds, the second-fastest high school time on record for that race. But a strained hamstring kept him out of action for the Shamrocks this spring until May 2, when he won both hurdles races at the Farmington Invitational. Brocks has signed with Ohio State and will study engineering.

Performance of the Week: Sterling Heights Stevenson's Olivia Buford

October 9, 2026

Share This Story
Facebook
Twitter
WhatsApp
SMS Text Message
Email
Print
Copy Link to Clipboard

Copy link

Click below to copy the link to your clipboard


Olivia Buford ♦ Sterling Heights Stevenson
Senior ♦ Swimming

Buford was named Swimmer of the Meet at the Macomb County Championships after setting meet and Macomb L'Anse Creuse North pool records in the 50-yard freestyle (23.95 seconds) and also winning the 100 butterfly (58.75) by more than five seconds. Her 50 time ranks fifth on the state's top times list this season, and her butterfly time ranks 17th for that race.

A two-time MHSAA Finals racer, Buford finished 10th in the 50 a year ago in Lower Peninsula Division 1 and also qualified in the butterfly in 2025. She's qualified for both races again this fall and is about a second off securing a Finals cut time in the 100 backstroke as well. Buford is deciding where she'll attend college but would like to continue swimming and intends to pursue a degree in pre-medical studies with aspirations of becoming a doctor.
